questions.prompt: What does Google's SynthID page say SynthID Text is not designed to do?

options.text: Block a determined attacker from doing harm by itself
options.explanation: Right. Google says SynthID Text "is not designed to directly stop motivated adversaries from causing harm". It makes misuse harder.

options.text: Make AI-generated content any harder to misuse
options.explanation: Google says it can make it harder to use AI-generated content for malicious purposes.

options.text: Work alongside other methods to cover more content types
options.explanation: Google says it can be combined with other approaches to give better coverage.

questions.prompt: An OpenAI check on an audio file has a synthid entry but no c2pa entry. Why?

options.text: The C2PA check failed on this file, so its entry was left out of the response
options.explanation: A failed check is not the reason. C2PA results apply to images.

options.text: The audio holds no credentials, so the API returned not_detected for that entry
options.explanation: The API omits checks that do not apply instead of returning not_detected.

options.text: C2PA results apply to images only, so the API leaves out checks that do not apply
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI says audio includes a SynthID result and the API omits checks that do not apply.

questions.prompt: OpenAI's check returns detected for a file. How should you treat it?

options.text: As a full record of every edit made to the file since it was created
options.explanation: OpenAI says detected is not a complete history of a file.

options.text: As evidence of one specific signal, not a complete history of the file
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI says to treat detected as evidence of a specific supported signal, not a complete history of a file.

options.text: As proof that no person changed the file after the AI made it
options.explanation: A detected signal does not record later edits. OpenAI calls it evidence of a specific signal only.
